subject: Post-call recap: Lumina Analytics POC scope, owners, and token economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron@lumina.ai>, Priya Sinha <priya@lumina.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Lumina Analytics POC scope, owners, and token economics

Hi Aaron / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we lock the POC: 

Call highlights
- Goal: validate Redwood can meet Lumina's throughput and latency targets for real-time insights on customer support transcripts, and estimate cost per active user.
- Primary KPIs discussed: p95 latency (target <= 300ms for 512-token requests), sustained throughput (100 qps aggregate), cost/token budget (~$0.003/token under optimized quantized path), and semantic quality (F1 on entity extraction >= 0.88 on your evaluation set).

Proposed POC scope (draft)
- Duration: 4 weeks (2-week ingest/benchmark + 2-week validation & ops run).
- Workloads: 50k sample transcripts (provided by Lumina) + synthetic high-concurrency replay to simulate spike loads.
- Success criteria: 1) p95 latency <= 300ms at 100 qps, 2) average inference cost <= $0.003/token (post-quantization), 3) entity extraction F1 >= 0.88, and 4) no more than 2 incidents causing >5% error rate in a 24-hr window.
- Ownership: Marissa (Sales) — POC project lead and customer liaison; Ben (Solutions) — infra config, benchmarks, and runbook; Monica (Customer Success) — onboarding, evaluation labeling, and acceptance tests.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft POC scope (lumina-poc-scope-v1.pdf) and a sample workload csv. Please review and let me know any immediate redlines.

Next steps
1) Lumina to confirm dataset delivery timeline (ideally by May 8).
2) Redwood to schedule kickoff and share repo + temp credentials.
3) Get necessary security paperwork queued (we noted SOC 2 evidence will be required — Monica will follow up).

If that looks good, I’ll convert this into an actionable milestone plan and share by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Aaron Li <aaron@lumina.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya@lumina.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Lumina Analytics POC scope, owners, and token economics

Marissa — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency: our 300ms p95 target is for per-request end-to-end inference (including network hop for a hosted deployment). Will Redwood's numbers assume network E2E or just GPU inference time? We need the former for our SLA evaluation.
2) Cost: $0.003/token is in line with our internal target but depends on peak vs. amortized throughput. Can you confirm whether this is steady-state pricing or includes burst capacity pricing assumptions?
3) Quality: the F1 >= 0.88 is acceptable — we will send a labeled sample set (2k records) for initial smoke tests. Full 50k will follow after NDA.

Data delivery: Priya can provide the smoke test set by Friday May 7. We can do NDA + SOW signatures next week.

Also, one ask: can you include an explicit rollback/fallback policy in the runbook (e.g., automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency/SLA is breached for >5 minutes)? That's a hard requirement for our production readiness assessment.

Best,
Aaron

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron@lumina.ai>, Priya Sinha <priya@lumina.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Lumina Analytics POC scope, owners, and token economics

Aaron — great questions and thanks for confirming data timing. Answers inline below and an updated action list: 

1) Latency scope: We will report both GPU-only inference time (for benchmarking) and an E2E measurement that includes network hop for a hosted deployment. For the E2E p95 target we will include a scoped network path (us-west region) and note cross-region variance. We’ll call out which metric is used for acceptance.

2) Cost assumptions: The $0.003/token estimate is for steady-state optimized quantized inference with continuous batching at target throughput. Burst pricing (when Autoscale adds extra capacity) may increase unit cost; we will model both steady and 2x burst scenarios in the cost appendix. 

3) Quality: thanks — Priya, once we have the 2k smoke labels Ben will run an initial quality pass and return precision/recall.

4) Fallback policy: yes — Redwood will provide a runbook section with automatic fallback to a compatible smaller-parameter variant and a regional reroute policy. The rule will be: if E2E p95 exceeds target for 5 continuous minutes OR error rate >5% for 3 minutes, system switches to fallback model and notifies ops. We’ll include play-by-play rollback steps and how to re-seed KV caches after a fallback.

Action items updated
- By May 7: Lumina deliver 2k smoke labels (Priya).
- By May 8: Redwood share kickoff calendar invite, repo access, and temporary API key (Marissa).
- By May 10: Ben to run initial benchmark on sample set and produce a short report (ben.carter@redwoodinference.com).
- By May 11: Monica to start security questionnaire (SOC 2 checklist) and list any additional documentation needed.

I’ve attached an updated scope PDF with the fallback clause noted. If everything looks good, we’ll convert this into a formal SOW and schedule the kickoff.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Li <aaron@lumina.ai>, Priya Sinha <priya@lumina.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Lumina Analytics POC scope, owners, and token economics

Quick technical note — ran a quick dry run on the 1k synthetic slice from the sample csv this morning. Preliminary observations: 
- With continuous batching at 100 qps equivalent, GPU inference p95 (local) is ~220ms for 512-token trimmed prompts using the quantized variant.
- Memory footprint suggests we can host two concurrent shard workers per A100-80GB equivalent.
- Cost modeling (rough) suggests $0.0025/token steady-state; burst up to $0.004/token at 2.5x autoscale. I’ll formalize these numbers in the benchmark report scheduled for May 10.

Note for runbook: we should specify cache warmup durations (estimate 3 minutes to reach steady-state KV hit rate for repeated sessions) — will add to ops section.

Ben
Lead Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
